problem: Find the radius of the curvature for the curve $r(t)=⟨{e}^{2t},\,{e}^{-t}⟩$ at $t=0.$

activity_context.topic_title: The Curvature of a Plane Curve

feedback.problem: Find the radius of the curvature for the curve $r(t)=⟨(1+t)^{2},\,{t}^{2}⟩$ at $t=0.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The curvature $κ(t)$ of a plane curve $r(t)=x(t)\,i+y(t)\,j$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{|{x}^{′}(t){y}^{″}(t)-{y}^{′}(t){x}^{″}(t)|}{([{x}^{′}(t)]^{2}+[{y}^{′}(t)]^{2})^{3/2}}.
$$

The radius of curvature $R$ is defined as
$R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}.$

Along our curve, we have

$$
x(t)=(1+t)^{2},\,y(t)={t}^{2}.
$$

First, we calculate the derivatives of the components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & =2(1+t),\, & {y}^{′}(t) & =2t \\ {x}^{″}(t) & =2,\, & {y}^{″}(t) & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting these into the formula for the curvature, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{|2(1+t)\cdot 2-2t\cdot 2|}{{(\,(2(1+t))^{2}+(2t)^{2})}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{4}{8{((1+t)^{2}+{t}^{2})}^{3/2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the curvature at $t=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(0) & =\frac{1}{2{((1+(0))^{2}+(0)^{2})}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2(1+0)^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the radius of curvature at $t=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(0) & =\frac{1}{κ(0)}=2.\end{aligned}
$$
